Before ru12-p29-examples, append three short items to the preparatory work: 'Factorise by taking out the common factor: (a) p+pq; (b) 3x+xy; (c) 7a−a.' Answers: p(1+q), x(3+y), a(7−1). Keep the complete review within one page.

[Pedagogy review · Suggestion · extension · pf-02a8df198b]
After ru13-p29-guided-d add parts: (i) Simplify (3^(n+3)−3^n)/3^(n+1). Answer: 26/3. (ii) Simplify (3^(n+3)−3^n)/3^(n−1). Answer: 78. (iii) Explain why changing n does not change either answer. Expected explanation: the numerator is 26×3^n, and division leaves fixed powers of 3.

[Pedagogy review · High priority · missing-prerequisite · pf-32ca0d4635]
Monic factorisation introduces P, S and F without stating the product-and-sum selection rule.
At ru23-p11-example-left: Before ru23-p11-examples-block add: 'For x²+bx+c, find two numbers whose product is c and whose sum is b. P means product, S means sum, and F records the chosen factor pair. Put these numbers into (x+…)(x+…).' Beside the first pair add: '(-4)(-9)=36 and -4+(-9)=-13.'
Also affects: ru23-p11-example-right, ru24-p11-guided-block

[Pedagogy review · Suggestion · variation-sequence · pf-ed19bff851]
At ru26-p25-guided-question: After part f add the single instruction: 'Predict which expressions are perfect squares.' Further parts: g x²+10x+25; h x²−10x+25; i x²+26x+25. Answers: (x+5)², (x−5)², (x+1)(x+25). Follow with unpatterned j 4x²−12x+9, answer (2x−3)². In g–i only the middle term varies; x² and 25 stay fixed. Part g deliberately repeats part a for this comparison.

[Pedagogy review · High priority · missing-prerequisite · pf-bbf6f2a140]

Before p26-example-1 add: 'Find the LCM of the numerical coefficients, then include each variable to the highest power appearing in either denominator.' Annotate the examples: 'LCM(5,a²)=5a²' and 'LCM(3x,5x)=15x: use coefficient 15 and one factor x.'
Also affects: p26-example-1, p26-example-2, p26-gp-c, p26-gp-e, p26-gp-f

[Pedagogy review · High priority · opening-review · pf-56cfe4851c]
Before p42-teaching add four short items: (a) Find the LCM of 3x and x². Answer: 3x². (b) Expand and simplify 3x²(1+1/(3x)), x≠0. Answer: 3x²+x. (c) Factorise 3x²+x and 3x²−3. Answers: x(3x+1), 3(x−1)(x+1). (d) Rewrite (a/b)÷(c/d) as multiplication and simplify, for b,c,d≠0. Answer: (a/b)×(d/c)=ad/(bc). Keep the review within one page.
Also affects: p42-example-1, p42-example-2
